summary.text: 備 is interpreted as a person carrying an arrow container, a scene associated with readiness. The simplified character 备 corresponds to 備 and commonly means “prepare” or “ready.”

formation.text: The traditional graph 備 is analyzed as phonosemantic: 人 depicts a person, while 𤰈 depicts an arrow container and is assigned a sound role in the received analysis. The carrying scene is linked to preparedness. The component’s sound role has no independently established historical reading comparison. 备 is the officially adopted simplified form corresponding to 備.

components.text: In 備, 人 depicts the person in the interpreted carrying scene associated with preparedness.

In 備, 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container, identified in texts as a quiver. The received analysis also assigns it a sound role, but no independent historical reading for the component is available to compare with 備.

sound_limitation.text: No independently retrieved historical reading for 𤰈 is available to compare with 備; 備’s own historical reconstruction does not establish the component’s pronunciation.

components.text: 备 is the officially adopted simplified form corresponding to 備. One account derives it from the variant 俻 by deleting 亻, but that specific route is not established by the official scheme.

history.text: 備 is recorded in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, though the cited accounts do not date its earliest appearance.

The right-hand component is printed as 𤰇 in some forms and is described as a changed form of seal-script 𤰈. Bronze forms also show its lower part changed to 用, tentatively interpreted as a sound element; a complete dated sequence is not established.
The 1956 simplification scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 was separately recognized as a variant of 備, but the scheme does not establish it as the direct source of 备.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation connects the graph with preparedness but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. Texts identify the pictured container as 箙, and 備 reportedly writes 箙 in a bronze inscription; neither fact establishes the pictured object’s original name or proves a sound match between that name and 𤰈.

備 is recorded with glosses including prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver scene may explain preparedness, but does not prove the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received Shuowen gloss is 慎也, “cautious” or “careful.” This dictionary gloss does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.

A bronze inscription reportedly uses 備 as a whole-graph loan for 箙, “quiver”: 備 was reused to write a different word on a proposed sound resemblance, rather than because “prepare” developed into “quiver.” That resemblance is not independently demonstrated, and the pictured object’s original name is unresolved.

overview.text: 備 is interpreted as a person carrying a quiver, a scene associated with being equipped and ready. The proposed reading of the picture as readiness does not prove the word’s earliest spoken meaning. 备 is the simplified form and commonly means “prepare” or “ready.”
